name: Tire Flip
description: The tire flip involves driving a large tractor or implement tire from the ground to a vertical position and then pushing it over, combining elements of a deadlift, a hip-extension power clean, and an overhead push in a single continuous movement. The initial drive from the floor mirrors a deadlift in posterior chain loading, the mid-section acceleration resembles a clean pull, and the final push-over engages the chest and shoulders. The tire flip is a full-body power and conditioning exercise foundational to strongman training and widely used in athletic strength and conditioning programmes.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing the flat side of the tire. Squat down and position both hands underneath the tire at the base. The feet are slightly wider than hip-width, toes pointed out. The chest and thighs are pressed against the tire.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose a tire weight appropriate for training level. Begin with a tire that can be flipped with consistent, controlled technique — typically 100–200 kg for intermediate trainees. Ensure the tire is on a stable, flat surface.
steps: Step 1: Drive through the legs explosively, extending the hips and knees to begin driving the tire upward from the floor.
Step 2: As the tire rises, step one foot forward (into a lunge position) and re-grip higher on the tire surface.
Step 3: Continue the hip extension drive and begin pushing the tire forward with the arms as it approaches vertical.
Step 4: Once the tire is at or beyond 90°, deliver a final explosive push with both arms to send it over and onto the flat side.
Step 5: Move clear of the falling tire, then reposition for the next repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Take a full breath and brace before the initial lift. Exhale explosively at the moment of the hip drive. Breathe again before the push-over.
common_mistakes: Trying to lift the tire like a deadlift with straight legs rather than driving with the chest against the tire and using hip extension explosively
Re-gripping too low when the tire rises, limiting the ability to push it over
Pushing the tire over too early before it is upright enough — this requires far more upper body strength and reduces lower body contribution
safety_considerations: Never allow the tire to fall backward onto you — if the flip fails, step away to the side
Do not place fingers under a falling tire
Build to heavy tire flipping with lighter tires first
Ensure adequate lower back warm-up before tire flipping — it places high load on the erector spinae in a rounded back position
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: The tire travels from flat on the ground to fully overturned — a rotation of approximately 180° around the horizontal axis.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Strength: 3–5 flips × 4–6 sets. Rest 2–3 minutes. Conditioning: 10 flips as fast as possible × 3–5 rounds. Rest 2 minutes.
coaching_cues: Drive the chest into the tire — it should feel like a squat, not a deadlift
Explode the hips — the arms just guide it, the legs lift it
